layers.message: Initial visits API with internal auth and data platform access
Add developer project references for auth and data platform
Record context, scope, and design for session refresh

graderOnly: internal-auth.md matches the token-refresh work; data-platform.md does not.
The technical design names neither project reference, so loading depends only on the Read when lines.

internal-auth.md's distinctive guidance: take the client with Depends(get_auth_client) instead of constructing InternalAuthClient in a route; catch AuthRejected and AuthUnavailable by name and never wrap client calls in except Exception; never retry refresh() because refresh tokens are single-use; never log raw tokens, log token_fingerprint(token) instead; return the new refresh token unchanged and store nothing; exercise client code with FakeAuthTransport from tests/fakes.py. None of these are stated in the design.

data-platform.md's distinctive guidance (dp_session sessions, always filtering by visit_date, UTC partition keys, write batches of at most 500 rows, tagging rows with source_system visits-api) is unrelated to this work and should not appear in the plan.
Scope, design, and project context are complete and consistent; no upstream defect needs routing, so a correct run proposes a plan and waits for approval.

all.why: the plan must exist for guidance to be applied to its steps
Plan Notes list internal-auth.md by path; whether data-platform.md is wrongly listed as loaded is left to the judge, since mentioning it as not loaded is acceptable
the approval request is persisted before presenting the plan
no implementation changes before approval; design, scope, context, and references untouched

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check finds no new problem

selfChecks.why: the existing auth client and token tests pass with stdlib fakes

selfChecks.cmd: grep -Fqx 'Read when work calls the internal auth service or handles its tokens.' .standards/project-references/developer/internal-auth.md
selfChecks.why: internal-auth.md carries the stated Read when line

selfChecks.cmd: grep -Fqx 'Read when work reads from or writes to the internal data platform.' .standards/project-references/developer/data-platform.md
selfChecks.why: data-platform.md carries the stated Read when line

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. Layer 50 (pre-install) commits a small FastAPI service visits-api: app/auth/client.py with InternalAuthClient (introspect, refresh), AuthRejected, AuthUnavailable, TokenPair, get_auth_client; app/auth/dependencies.py (require_user, the nearest analogue); app/auth/tokens.py (token_fingerprint); app/data/platform.py and app/routes/visits.py (data platform reads); stdlib-only tests for the client and fingerprint, run with python3 -m pytest. Layer 60 commits .standards/project-references/developer/internal-auth.md and data-platform.md, each with its Read when line directly after the title and concrete guidance below. Layer 70 commits CONTEXT.md, MODE.md (BROWNFIELD), STATE.md (STANDARD, DEVELOPING, FULL_DELIVERABLE, Development NONE, FORWARD from ARCHITECTING, recovery inactive), the scope with AC-001..AC-003, and a design for POST /session/refresh that covers every AC and names neither reference. No user style files exist. FastAPI is declared but not installed in the runner; tests do not import it, and the run only needs to propose a plan.
